headline: A shallow M7.7 earthquake struck the Azuero Peninsula at 12:56 local time on 9 October. SINAPROC reports no deaths or missing persons, 27 injured and 142 homes affected; damage across seven provinces.
key_points: Official (SINAPROC, 20:00 local): 0 deaths, 0 missing, 27 injured; 142 homes affected (3+ destroyed), 188 schools, 20 health facilities, 9 bridges.
Los Pozos (Herrera): mayor reports hundreds of homes collapsed — far above SINAPROC's 32 homes affected in Herrera; counts still rising.
Tonosí cut off by road; four people rescued from a hotel. Mariato communities cut off after road ruptures.
Penonomé: hotel, cathedral, Gobernación, churches and colonial houses damaged; Bolívar statue toppled.
Hospitals evacuated in San Félix (~209 people), Penonomé, Santiago and Las Tablas; 188 schools damaged nationwide (MEDUCA).
Water: Chilibre back to full production, supply returning gradually. No emergency declaration yet; CAF offers US$50M credit line. 95+ aftershocks.

areas.text: Partial collapse of Hotel Dos Continentes; San Juan Bautista cathedral tower fell onto a car; Gobernación wall collapsed; market damaged (1 injured); Hospital Aquilino Tejeira cracked and evacuated; Iguana Mall damaged.
Town cut off by road; four people rescued from a hotel, one woman with a broken arm (EFE). Homes collapsed; minor hospital damage. Strongest modelled shaking (MMI VIII–IX).
El Sitio hostel collapsed. Locals told La Prensa people were trapped, but local authorities say the damaged tourist buildings in Pedasí were unoccupied. No official confirmation of anyone trapped.
Cathedral and municipal building damaged (partial roof collapse); bus terminal and Policlínica Horacio Díaz Gómez damaged.
Soná fire station damaged; road to Torio (Mariato) split with vertical offsets; Santiago–Arenas road cut. M6.6 aftershock at 20:25 UTC centred 14 km W of Río Grande (Soná).
Part of the Basílica Menor tower collapsed.

areas.area: Los Pozos, Las Minas, Ocú & Chitré, Herrera
areas.text: Los Pozos mayor: hundreds of homes collapsed in 5 of 9 corregimientos; parish church ~70% destroyed; schools and roads damaged. Cracked homes in Las Minas; classroom ceiling collapse in Ocú; damage in Chitré.
Ceiling collapse in a school/university building (Telemundo video). Sunday Guardian, citing Telemetro, reports significant damage to at least six buildings — unconfirmed.
Broken windows on Calle 50 and Paitilla; hospitals evacuated as a precaution; Metro lines 1 and 2 suspended; Tocumen airport closed.
Considerable structural cracks at the Macaracas fire station (Fire Brigade via SINAPROC). Strong modelled shaking; few other reports so far.

Hospital del Oriente Chiricano (San Félix) fully evacuated, ~209 people (MINSA); damage at Puerto Armuelles hospital and Tolé health centre; cracked hotel facade and fire station in David; 15+ schools damaged. Shops and homes affected in the Pearl Islands; minor school damage in Darién.

services.text: Distribution outages in six provinces (Chiriquí, Herrera, Los Santos, Veraguas, Coclé, part of Panamá Oeste); 17 circuits restored in Colón. ETESA says the national transmission network is stable.

Treatment plants damaged nationwide; Chilibre (most of Panama City and San Miguelito) back to 70% after falling to 20%. CSS suspended hemodialysis nationwide due to water shortage; Monte Esperanza (Colón) tanks damaged but pumping.
Widespread mobile and internet failures across several operators.
Tocumen International closed and evacuated; flights diverted to Barranquilla, Cartagena, Bogotá, San José, Managua and Panamá Pacífico.
Road to Torio (Mariato) ruptured; Santiago–Arenas road cut; damage around Cambutal.
Operating normally; ACP denied rumours of damage to Agua Clara locks.
Classes suspended nationwide; University of Panama closed; public offices closed by presidential order.
PTWC initially warned of 1–3 m waves on Panama's coasts; later no Pacific-wide threat. No tsunami damage reported.
Panama City municipality suspended all municipal services, including markets, until further notice.

upcoming: President Mulino to fly to Tonosí today (Saturday); next SINAPROC update and MEDUCA decision on classes expected.
unknowns: Number of displaced people and people in shelters — only 8 families sheltered in Coclé reported so far.
Confirmed count of damaged and destroyed homes; Los Pozos 'hundreds collapsed' is the mayor's estimate.
Situation in cut-off communities (Tonosí, Mariato coast) and the hardest-shaken rural areas.
When water supply in Panama City and power in southern Veraguas will be restored.
Landslides in the hills of southern Azuero and Veraguas (one unconfirmed report near El Valle de Antón).
